I'm glad I bought a 3 pack I used 2 packages to make a good coupler set. The first one I drove on the motor split the zinc hub open and I had to open a second package to get another "spider" from the set. I have serviced these machines for years and have always used oem Whirlpool, I'll go back to Whirlpool if this one doesn't last. For those that complain about the tight fit, that's OK That's by design. When they are tapped in place I recommend a 9/16 socket placed on the metal hub, tap lightly with a hammer until seated this shears off the nubs inside the bore which are there to provide the tight fit. I also recommend replacing the motor mounts along with the coupler as the mounts settle with age and put stress on the coupler and motor bearings.

The agitator on our old whirlpool washer wasn't moving, and the tub didn't spin, but could hear the motor turning along with a little grinding noise, so checked the motor coupler and it had a crack in it.  Ordered this replacement part and it fit well, fairly easy to install.  This replacement part has metal inlays that will hopefully hold up better than the original, but the original lasted nearly twenty years!  Better to spend 7 dollars for a new coupling than 700 for a new washer!  Plenty of YouTube videos out there to figure out how to change it out.  Because of the metal inlays, you do have to tap firmly with a hammer and a block of wood or something to get the two parts to seat on the motor and the transmission.  Shipped quickly, arrived a day early, actually.
